aligned.stance_rationale: SSE supports accelerated renewable deployment, electricity-network investment and market reform, consistent with the Committee’s conclusions on flexible networks, grid infrastructure and REMA.
aligned.anchor_text: We will also deliver over 20% of the necessary upcoming electricity networks investment in the UK to connect renewable energy and enable electrification of heat and transport, alongside investment in critical technologies like carbon, capture and storage, hydrogen, solar and pumped storage hydro.
aligned.qualified_text: Our preliminary estimate, based on unaudited investment plans, is that we will also deliver over 20% of the necessary upcoming electricity networks investment in the UK to connect renewable energy and enable electrification of heat and transport, alongside investment in critical technologies like carbon, capture and storage, hydrogen, solar and pumped storage hydro.

opposed.stance_rationale: The Adam Smith Institute argues that variable renewables cannot meet the UK’s needs without substantial nuclear baseload and that much greater nuclear capacity is urgent, cutting against the Committee’s emphasis on flexibility, smart solutions and market reform to manage a renewables-led system.
opposed.anchor_text: On more than 180 days in any year wind only produces 4GW at some stage of the day or night; it therefore necessitates significant back up.
opposed.qualified_text: Preliminary data from Scotland only indicate that on more than 180 days in any year wind produces only 4GW at some stage of the day or night, necessitating significant back up.

spec.related_conclusion: Ofgem should review whether it has robust processes in place to monitor whether Distribution Network Operators are taking a 'Flexibility First' approach and making sufficient use of smart solutions.
